summary.intent: Push the branch, open an Entire trail and draft PR for a Depot CI change, monitor CI, then make the firmware change-detection script smarter (run firmware tests on PlatformIO/Pillow upgrades but not every pyproject.toml/uv.lock change) and pin key dev dependencies for Renovate to manage.
summary.outcome: Opened trail #278 and draft PR #180, moved the Linear ticket to In Review, and confirmed the `changes` job works on Depot (firmware=true). Implemented tools/firmware_changed.py with 14 new tests (TDD plus mutation check), pinned ty/pillow/pytest/machfs/pre-commit, relocked, and committed locally with the full tools suite passing (759); push held until CI finishes.

repo: The CI workflow (ci.yml) has a `changes` job that outputs `firmware=true|false` using `github.base_ref` and an `origin/$BASE_REF...HEAD` diff, gating the three `firmware-tests` shards via a `firmware-gate` job.
Plan is to make `firmware-gate` the required check and remove the three individual shard checks from branch protection.
Firmware tests take roughly 12-14 minutes across three shards on Depot CI.
Dependency pins are managed in pyproject.toml with uv.lock; Renovate is intended to handle explicit updates for pinned versions.
PR bodies in this repo start with a ticket line, so markdownlint MD041 (first line H1) is an expected, ignorable warning; the Entire hidden marker must be preserved when editing the body.

code.finding: New script decides whether firmware tests are due, now smart enough to detect PlatformIO or Pillow version changes in pyproject.toml/uv.lock rather than treating all changes to those files as firmware-relevant.
14 tests written first and confirmed failing before implementation, then mutation-checked against the script.

workflow: Trail did not sync the PR body, so the body had to be written manually with `gh pr edit` and read back to verify the draft state and hidden marker.
Pushing to the branch would cancel the in-progress CI run, so the commit was made locally and the push deferred until CI completes.
Use `depot ci` commands to list runs, view the job hierarchy and read individual job logs; a background wait can notify when a run finishes.
TDD with a red-first test run plus mutation checking was used to validate the new script.

friction: Trail did not sync the PR body, requiring a manual `gh pr edit`.
Pushing new commits would cancel the running CI, forcing the push to be held back.
The Depot log summary did not show pass/fail for lint, pre-commit and tools-tests, so only the `changes` log was verified.
CI shards take 12-14 minutes, requiring polling.
open_items: Push the local commit once the current CI run (v9mq4dj14f) finishes, and verify the `firmware-gate` pass line (changes/firmware_due/tests).
Exercise the skip path (firmware=false) with a follow-up PR that changes only tooling, docs or dependencies.
After CI is confirmed, make `firmware-gate` a required check and remove the three shard checks from branch protection.
Verify Renovate correctly handles the newly pinned versions of ty, pillow, pytest, machfs and pre-commit.
